scores.claim_text: As of December 31, 2023, Viking operated a fleet of 92 ships (81 river, 9 ocean, 2 expedition), itemized by named vessel.
scores.M_value: 'Viking Octantis' = 0 hits. 'Viking Holdings' = 19 hits but ALL are Roper Technologies (CIK 0000882835) referencing an unrelated 'Viking' software/insurance entity, not the cruise operator's fleet.
scores.interpretation: FOREIGN-ISSUER CAVEAT (Bermuda FPI; European/global fleet). No US federal registry covers cruise vessels operating outside the US. EPA FRS = US industrial facilities (n/a to ships); NHTSA = US motor vehicles (n/a); the one US-flagged exception (Viking Mississippi) is a chartered vessel, not owned. Distinctive vessel names return 0 in SEC full-text, which is expected and NOT a contradiction. The fleet is itemized vessel-by-vessel with IMO-class detail in the prospectus, internally consistent. Absence in US registries does not impugn the claim. UNVERIFIABLE per foreign-issuer calibration.

scores.claim_text: Largest contracted newbuild orderbook in the cruise industry: 18 river vessels by 2026, 6 ocean ships through 2028, plus options; ~42% of new luxury-ocean berth supply.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext search_term='Viking Vela' (named lead ocean newbuild) (cutoff 2024-05-02)
scores.interpretation: Newbuild orderbook is contracted at European/Italian shipyards (Fincantieri/Neptun-type yards) financed via European export-credit agencies — no US federal registry records foreign shipbuilding contracts. The named newbuilds (Viking Vela, Viking Vesta, Ship XIII-XVI) and river Longships are individually enumerated with per-ship prices and delivery dates in the financial-statement notes (Commitments & Contingencies), and tie to the $3.0B shipbuilding-obligation line in the contractual-obligations table — internally corroborated and quantified. The 'largest orderbook / 42% of supply' superlative cites third-party Cruise Industry News Orderbook data; it is a market-share claim (LOW-discriminative) not registry-recordable. UNVERIFIABLE in any US registry; no contradiction. Foreign-issuer caveat applies.

scores.claim_text: Secured shipyard newbuild financing: SACE Financing for up to 80% of ocean-ship contract prices; Hermes-guaranteed (95%) loans for eight Longships and two Longships-Seine river vessels.
scores.M_value: 'SACE' = 262 hits; top filers are direct cruise peers Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings (NCLH, CIK 0001513761) and NCL Corp (CIK 0001318742) disclosing SACE export-credit financing of newbuilds in their 10-Ks/8-Ks.
scores.interpretation: SACE (the Italian export-credit agency) is independently confirmed via counterparty/peer SEC disclosure as the standard mechanism for financing cruise newbuilds — exactly as Viking describes for its Fincantieri-built ocean ships. While these hits are peers (NCLH) rather than Viking itself (Viking is an FPI not in SEC full-text pre-IPO), they corroborate that the claimed financing structure is real, industry-standard, and not fabricated. The 80% LTV and export-credit-agency (SACE / Hermes/Euler Hermes) structure matches documented cruise-industry practice. PASS on mechanism corroboration; the specific loan tranches are internally detailed and consistent in the notes.

scores.claim_text: Held $3,486.6M of deferred revenue at Dec 31, 2023, reflecting significant advance customer bookings collected ahead of cruise dates.
scores.M_check: No external registry covers advance-booking / deferred-revenue balances; audited financial-statement figure only.
scores.M_value: Not registry-recordable. The $3,486.6M deferred-revenue figure is an audited IFRS balance (E&Y, unqualified) and is internally consistent across the liquidity discussion, working-capital deficit reconciliation, and cash-flow statement (deferred-revenue inflows of $335.2M in 2023).
scores.interpretation: Booking-curve / deferred-revenue claims are not in any federal registry (no counterparty discloses an aggregate consumer-booking balance). The figure is audited and internally cross-checks. The large working-capital deficit is the normal cruise-industry model (advance deposits recognized over the cruise period), not financial distress. UNVERIFIABLE — honestly scored; no manufactured severity.

scores.claim_text: Audited by Ernst & Young AS (PCAOB ID 1572), auditor since 2010, unqualified opinion.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext search_term='Ernst Young AS' (cutoff 2024-05-02); PCAOB ID 1572 self-disclosed in the audit report.
scores.M_value: E&Y AS (Oslo) is a PCAOB-registered firm (ID 1572) and signs the report dated in the prospectus; the audit opinion reproduced in the filing is a standard unqualified opinion under PCAOB standards with one critical audit matter (private-placement derivative fair value).
scores.interpretation: Big-Four PCAOB-registered auditor with a stated 14-year tenure and a clean opinion. The single CAM (PP derivative valuation) is properly a fair-value-estimation matter, not a going-concern or fraud flag. This is a positive honesty/governance signal. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Over 9,500 crewmembers from 90+ countries at 2023 peak; ~80% crew retention.
scores.M_check: No US registry covers a foreign cruise operator's global headcount (crew are non-US, on foreign-flagged ships); not in DOL/BLS US-employment registries.
scores.M_value: Not registry-recordable for a Bermuda FPI with non-US crew.
scores.interpretation: Headcount/retention is a soft operational metric with no independent US registry. Foreign-issuer caveat: US labor registries do not cover foreign-flagged-vessel crew. UNVERIFIABLE; not manufactured into severity.

scores.claim_text: Feb 2024 accommodation purchase agreement for all cabins on select Zhao Shang Yi Dun sailings (owned/operated by CMV China JV), 72 days Q3/Q4 2024.
scores.M_value: 'Zhao Shang Yi Dun' = 0 hits in SEC full-text.
scores.interpretation: A China JV (CMV) operating a Chinese-market coastal cruise ship is precisely the kind of foreign relationship no US counterparty discloses. The arrangement is described as forward (72 days in H2 2024, with extension options) — a planned/forward commitment, not a current operational obligation. Absence in US registries is expected, not a contradiction. UNVERIFIABLE per foreign-issuer + planned-vs-operational calibration.
